lines.vo: Why can't you focus with your phone right next to you?
That's not weak focus. That's the phone doing its job.
Kev tracks his phone free work blocks in his Break the Habit tracker.
lines.cap: Kev tracks his phone-free work blocks in his Break the Habit tracker.

lines.vo: In one study of about eight hundred people, phones sat face down on the desk, in a pocket, or in another room.
lines.cap: In one study of about 800 people, phones sat face down on the desk, in a pocket, or in another room.

lines.vo: People whose phone was in another room did noticeably better on memory and focus tests.
Just having it nearby seemed to pull on their attention, even when they never touched it.
Later studies found smaller effects, but out of sight is still an easy win.
Phone in the other room, box checked. That's how you stay on track.
